title: Return of Frustratingly Easy Unsupervised Video Domain Adaptation
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Separating static from temporal features in a shared encoder and subtracting them isolates the temporal signal that transfers across domains.
layout: Single row, left-to-right, dashed module boxes, two parallel streams in the center
description: A wide left-to-right pipeline made of dashed boxes. On the far left are two stacks of video frames, a source clip and a target clip, labeled X^S and X^T. They feed an Encoder drawn as stacked 3D slabs. Next come stacked source features (orange/yellow) and target features (blue). The large central dashed box is the Temporal-Static Subtraction Module. Inside it, a blue dashed first stream adds positional embeddings, passes through self-attention blocks, and produces temporal representations. A red dashed second stream has no positional embeddings. It passes through the same self-attention blocks and then average pooling, and produces static representations. Blue and red arrows converge on a circled subtraction symbol. The output goes to the right-hand box, where feature stacks are tied to the adversarial loss L_adv and the classification loss L_cls by arrows. Bold black block arrows link the stages.
caption: MetaTrans overview. The input videos are fed into an encoder to extract visual features, followed by a temporal-static subtraction module to learn a static representation and a temporal representation from the visual features without and with positional embeddings, respectively. A latent temporal embedding is obtained by subtracting the static features from temporal ones.
abstract: Unsupervised video domain adaptation (UVDA) is a practical but under-explored problem. In this paper, we propose a frustratingly easy UVDA method, called MetaTrans. Specifically, MetaTrans adopts a concise learning objective that contains only two fundamental loss terms. Despite the simplicity of the learning objective, MetaTrans embodies an advanced UVDA idea, that is, handling the spatial and temporal divergence of cross-domain videos separately, through a subtle model architecture design. By implementing a temporal-static subtraction module, MetaTrans effectively removes spatial and temporal divergence. Extensive empirical evaluations, particularly on various cross-domain action recognition tasks, show substantial absolute adaptation performance enhancement and significantly superior relative performance gain compared with state-of-the-art UVDA baselines.
